[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Accessibility (A11y): ARIA Attributes and Semantic HTML"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Accessibility, often abbreviated as A11y (as there are 11 letters between the 'A' and the 'y'), is the practice of making web content usable by as many people as possible. This includes people with disabilities, such as visual, auditory, motor, or cognitive impairments. Semantic HTML and ARIA attributes are crucial tools for building accessible web applications."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"Semantic HTML"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Semantic HTML uses HTML elements to convey meaning and structure to the content of a webpage, rather than just its presentation. This helps assistive technologies, like screen readers, understand the content and provide a better user experience."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Common Semantic HTML Elements"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"

"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Using semantic HTML elements provides structure and meaning to your content, making it easier for screen readers and other assistive technologies to interpret and present the information to users with disabilities. It also improves SEO and maintainability."},{"order":16,"type":"heading","text":"ARIA Attributes"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"ARIA (Accessible Rich Internet Applications) is a set of attributes that you can add to HTML elements to provide additional semantic information to assistive technologies. ARIA attributes are especially useful when HTML alone is not sufficient to convey the meaning or functionality of a UI element, particularly with dynamic content and custom widgets."},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Key ARIA Attributes"},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"role: Defines the purpose of an element. For example, role="button", role="navigation", role="alert"."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"aria-label: Provides a text label for an element when a visible label is not present. Use sparingly, and prefer visible labels when possible."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"aria-labelledby: References another element on the page that serves as the label for the current element. This is preferred over aria-label when a visible label exists."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"aria-describedby: References another element on the page that provides a description for the current element."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"aria-hidden: Hides an element from assistive technologies. Use this to hide purely decorative elements."},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"aria-live: Indicates that an element will be updated dynamically, and instructs assistive technologies to announce those updates. Values include 'off', 'polite', 'assertive'."},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"aria-atomic: Used with aria-live, indicates whether the entire region should be considered when announcing changes."},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"aria-relevant: Used with aria-live, indicates what types of changes are relevant and should be announced (e.g., 'additions', 'removals', 'text')."},{"order":27,"type":"bullet_point","text":"aria-expanded: Indicates whether a collapsible element is currently expanded or collapsed."},{"order":28,"type":"bullet_point","text":"aria-disabled: Indicates that an element is perceivable but disabled, so it is not editable or otherwise operable."},{"order":29,"type":"subheading","text":"ARIA Examples"},{"order":30,"type":"code","text":""},{"order":31,"type":"paragraph","text":"In this example, a button is given the role of 'button' because it might not be a native HTML button element. ARIA should be a last resort when semantic HTML is insufficient."},{"order":38,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Avoid redundant ARIA attributes. Don't use ARIA attributes that duplicate the functionality of native HTML elements."},{"order":39,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Test your website with screen readers and other assistive technologies to ensure it is accessible."},{"order":40,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Keep ARIA attributes up-to-date with the state of your application. For example, update aria-expanded when a collapsible element is expanded or collapsed."},{"order":41,"type":"paragraph","text":"By combining semantic HTML with ARIA attributes, you can create web applications that are more accessible and usable for everyone."}]
